message.reasoning_content: We need solve: price chips 40¢ each. Candies 75¢ each. George spent $5 = 500¢. He got 3 bags of chips: cost 3*40=120¢. He kept 1% of his money? Means he kept 1% of his money after spending? He spent 500¢ total? Wait: He spent $5 and got 3 bags of chips and kept 1% of his money. Means he had some money, spent some on chips and candies, and kept 1% of his money (maybe leftover). Let x = number of candy bars. Total spent = 120 + 75x. He kept 1% of his money: meaning he had some initial amount M, spent 500? Actually he spent $5 total. So M = 500¢. He kept 1% of his money: meaning after spending, he had 1% of 500 = 5¢ left? But he spent 500? Contradiction. Maybe he spent 5 dollars and kept 1% of his money meaning he had 5 dollars, spent some, and kept 1% of his money as leftover? So leftover = 0.01*500=5¢. So spent = 500-5=495¢. So 120+75x=495 => 75x=375 => x=5. So answer 5.
